text: The paper's remaining residue is a combination rather than a primitive, and it is not compared with the nearest sequential peer-prediction, prediction-market, staking, or debate mechanisms.
citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Reinforcement Learning from Reputation Feedback (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=7456999
abstract: Even that residue is a combination rather than a primitive, and the paper does not clear it against the mechanisms nearest to it. Sequential peer prediction, prediction markets with a revision stage, staking and slashing designs from distributed consensus, and iterated debate all combine a free elicitation stage with a costly commitment stage in some form, and this paper does not compare against any of them.
